content.text: Other recommended IV regimens: cefotetan 2 g IV q12h or cefoxitin 2 g IV q6h, each + doxycycline 100 mg PO/IV q12h; give doxycycline orally when possible (IV infusion is painful)
Alternative IV regimens: ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g IV q6h + doxycycline; or clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h + gentamicin (2 mg/kg load, then 1.5 mg/kg q8h, or 3–5 mg/kg once daily)
Other IM/oral regimens: cefoxitin 2 g IM + probenecid 1 g PO, or another parenteral third-generation cephalosporin, each + doxycycline + metronidazole x14 days

Cephalosporin allergy with low gonorrhea risk: levofloxacin 500 mg or moxifloxacin 400 mg PO daily + metronidazole x14 days, or azithromycin + metronidazole; quinolone regimens otherwise aren't recommended (resistant N. gonorrhoeae)
Metronidazole adds anaerobic coverage and also treats BV, which often accompanies PID
